Bug_Title: RV: Bad attempt to compute absolute value of signed 32-bit hashcode (RV_ABSOLUTE_VALUE_OF_HASHCODE)
Bug_Details:
This code generates a hashcode and then computes
the absolute value of that hashcode.  If the hashcode
is Integer.MIN_VALUE, then the result will be negative as well (since
Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) == Integer.MIN_VALUE).
 One out of 2^32 strings have a hashCode of Integer.MIN_VALUE,
including "polygenelubricants" "GydZG_" and ""DESIGNING WORKHOUSES".
 Integer.MIN_VALUE Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) == Integer.MIN_VALUE
Bug_Explanation: The code calculates the absolute value of a hash code generated from a string. The bug occurs because if the hash code is Integer.MIN_VALUE, then Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) returns Integer.MIN_VALUE, which is negative.
Trigger_Explanation: The test cases call the method `showBug` with strings known to produce a hash code of Integer.MIN_VALUE. This triggers the bug as the `Math.abs` of Integer.MIN_VALUE remains negative, causing the assertion expecting a non-negative result to fail.
